title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor Circuit
plain: On a turbocharged or supercharged engine, there's an electrical problem with a pressure sensor in the boosted intake air path. The computer uses it to control boost, so power may be limited.

causes.name: Unplugged, oily or corroded sensor connector

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the intercooler piping or throttle body
Measure the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal
fix: Repair the connector or wiring, or replace the pressure sensor.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: On a boosted engine, the intake pressure sensor's readings don't match what the computer expects. Often there's a boost leak, or the sensor is reading wrong.

causes.name: Boost leak from a loose clamp or cracked intercooler hose

checks: Inspect intercooler hoses and clamps for leaks or oil residue
Compare the sensor reading with key on, engine off to the barometric pressure reading
Smoke- or pressure-test the boost system
fix: Fix any boost leak first; replace the pressure sensor if readings stay wrong.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
plain: On a boosted engine, the intake pressure sensor's signal is lower than its normal range, usually from a wiring or connector problem or a failed sensor.

causes.name: Signal wire open or shorted to ground, or lost 5-volt reference

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Measure the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the pressure sensor.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor Circuit High
plain: On a boosted engine, the intake pressure sensor's signal is higher than its normal range, usually from a short in the wiring, a bad ground or a failed sensor.
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring for damage
Check the sensor ground and signal voltage with the engine off
fix: Repair the wiring or ground, or replace the pressure sensor.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: On a boosted engine, the intake pressure sensor's signal keeps dropping out or jumping, usually from a loose connection or a failing sensor.
symptoms: Occasional loss of power or limp mode
checks: Wiggle-test the connector and harness while watching the live reading
Clean any oil out of the connector
fix: Repair the connection or wiring; replace the sensor if the signal still jumps.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: There's a problem with the front oxygen sensor on bank 1, the one before the catalytic converter. It tells the computer whether the engine is running rich or lean.

causes.name: Damaged or burned wiring near the exhaust

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring where it runs near hot exhaust parts
Look and listen for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Watch the live sensor reading; a healthy one switches quickly between rich and lean
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring or exhaust leak repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 is stuck reading low, which looks like a very lean (too much air) mixture. It can be a real lean condition or a bad sensor or wire.

causes.name: Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor pulling in outside air
Real lean condition from a vacuum leak or low fuel pressure

checks: Check for exhaust leaks at the manifold and front pipe
Look at fuel trims; high positive trims point to a real lean condition
Inspect the sensor wiring for melted or rubbed spots
fix: Fix exhaust or vacuum leaks first; otherwise replace the upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 is stuck reading high, which looks like a very rich (too much fuel) mixture. It can be a real rich condition or a shorted or contaminated sensor.
symptoms: Possible black smoke or fuel smell

causes.name: Failed or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Signal wire shorted to the heater or another voltage source
Real rich condition from a leaking injector or high fuel pressure
Coolant or oil burning and fouling the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring for melted spots where wires could touch
Look at fuel trims; strongly negative trims point to a real rich condition
Check for coolant loss or oil burning
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor; fix any real rich condition first.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 is reacting too slowly to changes in the exhaust. This is usually a sign that the sensor is worn out.
symptoms: Usually no obvious change in driving

causes.name: Aged or worn upstream oxygen sensor
Sensor contaminated by oil, coolant or fuel additives
Vacuum leak or other fuel mixture problem

checks: Watch the live sensor reading; a healthy one switches rich and lean several times a second at steady 2,500 rpm
Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check for oil burning or coolant loss
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 isn't sending any changing signal at all. The sensor may be dead, unplugged, or its heater may not be working.

causes.name: Open circuit in the sensor wiring
Sensor heater not working, so the sensor never warms up

checks: Check that the sensor connector is plugged in and clean
Check for heater circuit codes and the heater fuse
Watch the live reading on a warm engine; a flat reading means no activity
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 has a built-in heater so it starts working quickly. This code means that heater or its wiring has a problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Slightly worse fuel economy after cold starts

causes.name: Burned-out heater inside the oxygen sensor
Damaged wiring or connector near the exhaust
Faulty heater control in the engine computer

checks: Check the fuse that powers the oxygen sensor heaters
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor connector
Inspect the sensor wiring for melted or chafed spots
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor; check the fuse and wiring first.
examples: Very common at high mileage as the heater element inside the sensor burns out

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: There's a problem with the rear oxygen sensor on bank 1, the one after the catalytic converter. It mainly checks that the converter is doing its job.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car for damage or corrosion
Check for exhaust leaks near the converter
Watch the live sensor reading on a warm engine
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 is stuck reading low (lean). Often an exhaust leak is letting in outside air, or the sensor has failed.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Look and listen for exhaust leaks around the converter and sensor
Inspect the wiring under the car for damage
Check fuel trims for a real lean condition
fix: Fix any exhaust leak; otherwise replace the downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 is stuck reading high (rich). The sensor may be shorted or contaminated, or the engine may really be running rich.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failed or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring under the car
Check fuel trims for a real rich condition
Watch the live reading; a reading pinned above 1 volt points to a short
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 is reacting too slowly when the fuel mixture changes, which usually means the sensor is aging.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Sensor contaminated by oil or coolant

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the converter
Watch how quickly the rear sensor reacts during a sudden throttle change or deceleration
Check for oil burning or coolant loss
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from rich to lean, such as when you lift off the gas.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Watch the rear sensor drop toward lean during a coast-down from highway speed
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from lean to rich, such as when you press the gas after coasting.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Watch the rear sensor rise toward rich when accelerating after a coast-down
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from rich to lean, such as when you lift off the gas.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Watch the rear sensor drop toward lean during a coast-down from highway speed
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from lean to rich, such as when you press the gas after coasting.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Watch the rear sensor rise toward rich when accelerating after a coast-down
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from rich to lean. It's usually a sign of an aging sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from lean to rich. It's usually a sign of an aging sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 isn't sending any changing signal. It may be dead, unplugged, or its heater may have failed.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Open circuit in the wiring under the car

checks: Check that the sensor connector is plugged in and not corroded
Check for heater circuit codes and the heater fuse
Watch the live reading on a warm engine; a flat reading near 0.45 volts means no activity
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain: The heater inside the rear oxygen sensor on bank 1, which helps it warm up quickly, or the heater's wiring has a problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Burned-out heater inside the oxygen sensor
Damaged wiring or connector under the car
Faulty heater control in the engine computer

checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor connector
Inspect the wiring under the car for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor; check the fuse and wiring first.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: Some vehicles have a third oxygen sensor further down the exhaust. This code means there's a problem with that sensor on bank 1 or its wiring.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector under the car

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 1 is stuck reading low (lean), often from an exhaust leak or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Inspect the wiring under the car
fix: Fix any exhaust leak; otherwise replace the oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 1 is stuck reading high (rich), usually from a shorted or contaminated sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Inspect the wiring under the car
Check fuel trims for a real rich condition
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 1 is reacting too slowly, which usually means the sensor is aging.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Watch how the sensor responds to throttle changes
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 1 isn't sending any changing signal, so it may be dead or disconnected.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the sensor connector and wiring under the car
Check for heater codes and the heater fuse
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: The heater inside the third oxygen sensor on bank 1, or its wiring, has a problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor connector
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor; check the fuse and wiring first.

title: Fuel Delivery Error
plain: The fuel system isn't delivering the amount of fuel the computer asked for. This code is mostly seen on diesel engines and can cause power loss or stalling.

causes.name: Clogged fuel filter or weak lift pump
Air getting into the fuel lines
Worn injection pump or faulty fuel quantity control
Wiring fault to the pump control

checks: Replace or check the fuel filter and drain any water
Check fuel supply pressure and look for air in the fuel lines
fix: Often a fuel filter or lift pump; worn injection pumps need repair or replacement.

title: Fuel Timing Error
plain: Fuel isn't being injected at the right moment. This is mostly a diesel code and usually points to a problem with the injection pump's timing control.
symptoms: Hard starting, rough running or smoke

causes.name: Faulty injection timing control on the pump
Injection pump timing set wrong after service
Faulty crank or pump position sensor
Low fuel supply or air in the fuel

checks: Check for related sensor or fuel supply codes
Have a shop compare desired and actual injection timing on a scan tool
fix: Repair the timing control, correct pump timing, or repair or replace the injection pump.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from rich to lean. It's usually a sign of an aging sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from lean to rich. It's usually a sign of an aging sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Aged or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from rich to lean. Because this sensor guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Fuel mixture problem such as a leaking injector

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from lean to rich. Because this sensor guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Fuel mixture problem such as a vacuum leak

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from rich to lean. Because this sensor guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Fuel mixture problem such as a leaking injector

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 is slow to react when the exhaust changes from lean to rich. Because this sensor guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Fuel mixture problem such as a vacuum leak

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.
